editorial.marketOverview: The semiconductor-led rout intensified late Friday morning. Reuters described the Nasdaq down 1.74%, S&P 500 down 1.01% and Philadelphia semiconductor index down roughly 6%, with AMD falling around 10% and Broadcom around 7%. These are intraday reported levels, not closing prices, and the precise quote times are not provided.
editorial.whatChanged: Relative to the 11:10 assessment, Nasdaq weakness grew from 1.42% to a reported 1.74%, while SOX fell from roughly 5% to roughly 6%. The newly cited AMD and Broadcom losses indicate broad semiconductor selling. This extends the material deterioration already flagged earlier today rather than creating a distinct new directional regime. Curated Open Watch remains at 163 entries.
editorial.marketInterpretation: The market's negative response to AI-sector uncertainty is stronger than the initial relief from slightly softer monthly producer inflation. Severe SOX underperformance is a confirmed sector narrative, but claims about simultaneous rates, volatility or commodity confirmation would be unsupported because fresh aligned data are unavailable. The previously reported 10Y and 2Y imply a +29.1 basis-point curve spread, not a contemporaneous market observation.
editorial.threeDayPath: Friday November 13 remains exposed to a weak close and possible de-risking into the weekend. Monday November 16 is the crucial test of semiconductor-led continuation versus an oversold reversal; Tuesday November 17 may be volatile as investors reassess AI funding and rates. The expected path is bearish with elevated downside risk, but a rebound remains plausible if breadth and chip leadership recover.
editorial.bullCase: A durable reversal would require Nasdaq and QQQ to reclaim lost ground, SOX to stop underperforming and recover, breadth to broaden and rates/volatility to ease at aligned observation times. Softer monthly PPI and selected strong earnings provide possible offsets, not proof of a bottom.
editorial.bearCase: The roughly 6% SOX decline and double-digit AMD weakness point to selling spreading beyond a single megacap. If the sector closes weak and breadth remains negative, follow-through selling on Monday becomes more plausible. The reported 10-year yield near 5.13% is an additional valuation constraint but is not synchronized with late-morning equities.
